requirement.description: The setup_unix_local_socket function incorrectly rejects socket paths containing null bytes, particularly in abstract namespace sockets (paths starting with '@'). This causes multiple test failures related to socket path validation.

contract.description: The function should properly handle socket paths that contain null bytes, distinguishing between valid abstract namespace usage (where null bytes are acceptable) and invalid paths that should be rejected.

inputs.input: path: None | str | bytes | PathLike[Any] - the socket path to validate
mode: int | None - permissions to set on the socket

outputs.output: socket.socket - a properly initialized UNIX socket

exceptions.exception: ValueError - raised when abstract Unix socket path contains null bytes (for invalid cases)

behavior.behavior: Paths starting with '@' (abstract namespace) should be allowed to contain null bytes as they are valid in this context
Regular socket paths should not contain null bytes, and if they do, should raise ValueError
System-level validation should be performed correctly without rejecting valid abstract paths

acceptance.acceptance: Tests in test_sockets.py that are failing with "embedded null byte" or "embedded null character in path" errors should pass
Specifically, tests with abstract namespace paths (marked with "abstract" parametrization) should work correctly
